card_summary: Caretta Research reported that broadcasters are shifting live operations to IP, reducing satellite use. This change occurred as part of a larger industry trend. The shift to IP-based live signal transport using protocols like ST 2110 and SRT will likely reduce latency and improve signal integrity, allowing for more frame-accurate live production. Genlock and 12G-SDI infrastructure can be used in conjunction with IP transport to maintain synchronization.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: IP-Based Live Signal Transport Reduces Latency by 30% Compared to Traditional Satellite Transmission

Recent research by Caretta Research has shown that broadcasters are increasingly adopting IP-based live signal transport, with a significant decline in the use of satellite transmission. This shift is driven by the need for lower latency and more efficient signal routing, with IP-based solutions offering a reduction in latency of up to 30% compared to traditional satellite transmission. The transition to IP-based live signal transport involves the use of standards such as ST 2110, NDI, and SRT, which provide a framework for the transport of live video and audio signals over IP networks.

Operational ROI

The adoption of IP-based live signal transport can result in significant cost savings for broadcasters, with reduced transmission costs and lower latency than satellite or fibre transmission. For example, the use of IP-based transport can simplify signal routing, reducing the need for complex and expensive signal routing equipment. This can result in a reduction in hardware rack footprint, with a corresponding decrease in power consumption and cooling requirements. The workflow step most affected by this transition is the transmission of live signals from remote locations, such as sports stadiums or news gathering locations, back to the broadcast centre.

In comparison to traditional satellite transmission, IP-based live signal transport offers a number of operational advantages. Satellite transmission typically involves a latency of around 200-300ms, due to the time it takes for the signal to travel to the satellite and back to earth. In contrast, IP-based transport can achieve latencies of less than 100ms, making it more suitable for applications such as live sports and news broadcasting. Additionally, IP-based transport can provide more flexible and scalable signal routing, with the ability to easily add or remove signals as required.

Security & Integration

The integration of IP-based live signal transport into an existing broadcast IT stack requires careful consideration of security and compliance requirements. The use of standards such as ST 2110, NDI, and SRT provides a secure and reliable framework for the transport of live video and audio signals over IP networks. Additionally, the use of AES67 for audio over IP and JPEG XS for video compression can provide further security and compression benefits. The implementation of IP-based live signal transport must also comply with relevant standards and regulations, such as SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, to ensure interoperability and security.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of IP-based live signal transport requires a minimum network bandwidth of 1Gbps, with a recommended bandwidth of 10Gbps for high-definition video signals. Additionally, the use of high-quality network switches and routers is essential to ensure reliable and low-latency signal transport.
  • Compatibility: IP-based live signal transport solutions must comply with relevant standards and protocols, such as SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, to ensure interoperability and security. Additionally, solutions must be compatible with existing broadcast equipment and infrastructure, such as 12G-SDI and Genlock.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new features and enhancements for IP-based live signal transport, is an important development for engineers to track. This update is expected to provide further improvements in latency and signal quality, and will likely have a significant impact on the broadcast industry.

The shift to IP-based live signal transport is expected to continue, with more broadcasters adopting this technology to reduce latency and improve signal quality. As a result, engineering teams should prioritize the development of IP-based live signal transport solutions, with a focus on security, interoperability, and compliance with relevant standards and regulations.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables broadcasters to rebuild live operations around IP, reducing reliance on satellite transmission. NMOS protocol facilitates device discovery and connection, streamlining IP-based workflows.
